preamble: Each claim states what it covers, what kind of evidence stands behind it, and what it does not show. Evidence classes: implementation (the code or document exists), automated (a test or probe in this repository), system (observed in a real system), human (a recorded observation), comparative (matched measurement against an alternative). A claim is `supported` only with automated or system evidence; it is marked verified only with system evidence at an exact revision. Automated evidence carries the commit at which its tests were last run green; any later change to its cited path makes it a candidate for re-running (`node scripts/claim-ledger.mjs --check --stale`). No claim in the first seeding had system-class evidence at a known revision. The 2026-10-16 re-check (X7) re-ran every cited test at 477529a and added claims for later work at the level reached; three carry production evidence at an exact revision and are marked verified. The check runs in CI. Publication, tag and visibility decisions are not made by this file.

evidence.test: flag wins over env and config
an empty SHIP_MODEL falls through to config, then the default

claims.claim: glm-5.3 resolved 35 of 50 seeded SWE-bench Lite instances.
claims.scope: Seeded 50-of-300 Lite subset, official evaluator, bare configuration (not the product path), recorded 2026-08-16. Not a Ship product result and not a held-out result.

claims.claim: With SHIP_LOOK=1 and SHIP_LOOK_IMAGE_MODEL=zai/glm-5.3-flash, a production run recorded text accessibility look steps and one image look under the cap, and the facts it reported matched the live page.
claims.scope: One completed soak run (run-9d75d86d) against example.com on the production instance at the receipt's revision, native harness, zai/glm-5.3, postgres store, publication parked at approve-merge and approved by the operator.

evidence.test: runLook: url then snapshot comes back as the observation, parameters riding the script
the open-tier refusal names the D3 rule: plan review, operator decision, no in-run workaround

limitations: n = 1 completed run on one public page; not a quality or reliability measure.
Vision routing is inferred from the next model turn describing a pixel-only fact; the gateway's own usage count for the flash model was not read.
The no-PR-attachment rule for look screenshots (D4) is unit-tested only; it was not visually confirmed on the forge PR.
Production now runs a later revision (03748ab) than the one soaked; the look code did not change between them, but that run was not repeated.

claims.claim: A run whose recorded input carries look is admitted as a browser resource class: its memory limit is raised by the measured browser delta and admission accounts for it, while plain runs are unchanged.
claims.scope: src/resource-class.ts and the worker's admission seams. Applies only to runs enqueued with SHIP_LOOK set.

evidence.test: a browser run's resolved limit carries the delta on every base, a plain run's is unchanged
flag-off equivalence: a plain run's overrides carry no class and are shape-identical to before
the raised limit reaches the daemon and the class itself never does

limitations: Not verified live on a memory-squeezed host. The soak's look run was admitted with this code present, but the receipt does not record the raised limit or any hold.
The 512 MB delta is the top of one measured page's overhead, not a measured ceiling; the pids limit is unchanged and unmeasured for multi-page sites.
Placement enforcement is still shadow-only.

claims.scope: src/delegate.ts and the durable delegate action. Default off; scans and children never get delegation.

evidence.test: spawn is idempotent per (parent, turn) and the cap is hard per task root
a delegate action parks on the child and merges its transfer back as the observation
enqueue materialises SHIP_DELEGATE and suppresses it for scans and children

limitations: Merged but not enabled in production; no live delegation run is recorded.
Tests use scripted models and in-memory stores.

claims.scope: src/bootstrap-admin.ts at web boot. File, nucleus and postgres runtimes.

evidence.test: an install with existing principals is skipped entirely, even with the env set
the password never appears in any log line, result, or refusal reason
nucleus runtime: two web processes on one store — the KV setNX decides, the loser creates nothing

limitations: The live evidence is the production observation recorded in AUDIT_OPEN (2026-10-16 bootstrap entry: one log line naming the user, on the postgres store), not a standalone receipt file.

claims.scope: --store postgres / SHIP_STORE=postgres (src/nucleus-pgwire.ts postgres dialect). Production web and worker run on it.

evidence.test: postgres setNX acquires once and refuses a live holder, TTL lapse re-opens the key
postgres streams round-trip fields in insertion order, per stream
the postgres dialect reaches the store from nucleusRuntime; nucleus stays the default
